confirmed_findings.summary: saveUnchained detects a lineage break at markSaved/noteDiskSynced (the new expectGen guard) but discards that knowledge: it still runs clearNetIf + onSuccess and still returns ok:true, so a write composed from a model that no longer exists is reported to every caller as a successful save of the current note.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A note's save fails (locked .md) → save-health banner. The ~10s auto-retry fires (store.ts:520 retrySaveFailure → saveNoteSession): compose captures gen=G, version=12, content C; setNet(P,C); await write(P,C) — the lock has just cleared so this write WILL succeed, but it is still parked on the await. During that window the user clicks 'Discard my changes' → discardFailedSave (store.ts:617) → reloadTabsFromDisk([P],{discardLocalEdits:true}) → openNoteModel(t.id,P,D) mints a NEW model (gen=G') holding the disk version D the user chose to keep, then clearWriteAhead(P) + clearSaveFailure(P). The write now resolves: markSaved (noteModel.ts:568) and noteDiskSynced (noteModel.ts:644) both refuse on gen ≠ G' — correctly — but line 271 clearNetIf and line 272 onSuccess run anyway and line 273 returns r with ok:true. Net result: the .md on disk now holds C (the bytes the user explicitly discarded), version D is overwritten and gone, the screen and the model still show D and report CLEAN, the failure banner is cleared, and afterDurableSave has reindexed note_meta/notes_fts and re-embedded note_embeddings from C. The write is gate-written/watcher-suppressed so no adopt event heals it. Nothing is surfaced anywhere: the user's explicit discard decision is silently inverted on disk and the disk version they chose to keep is destroyed.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, reachable, and silent. Interleaving verified against the actual code: retrySaveFailure (store.ts:520-533, driven by the always-enabled Retry button SaveHealthBanner.svelte:60 and the 10s auto-retry +layout.svelte:1761-1767) composes gen=G/content C and parks on await write; write_gate.rs:270-288 keeps a to-be-successful write parked ~0.5s+ (bounded replace retry with 50/100/150/200ms sleeps, plus create+sync_all on the very drive that caused the banner). discardFailedSave (store.ts:617-640) is serialized against nothing: saveChains (noteSession.ts:206) chains saves only, markCascading/markReseeding gate NoteEditor flushes (NoteEditor.svelte:287) not an already-awaiting save, and retrySaveFailure is ungated. Its reloadTabsFromDisk reads via read_note = bare fs::read_to_string with NO gate lock (libraries.rs:929-936), so it returns the pre-write bytes D1. The re-seed genuinely fires: reloadTabsFromDisk:1155 skips only when newContent === t.content, and tab.content is never updated by an ordinary save (handleSave NoteEditor.svelte:314-316 and handleFlush :452 don't touch it), so after any earlier successful autosave it is stale -> openNoteModel at :1159 mints gen G', :1168/:638 clear the net, :639 clears the banner. The parked write then lands: markSaved/noteDiskSynced correctly refuse on gen mismatch, but noteSession.ts:271-273 still runs clearNetIf + onSuccess and returns ok:true. Result: disk holds C (the bytes the user explicitly discarded), the disk version D1 the user chose to keep is overwritten and exists only in an in-memory model that reports CLEAN and will therefore never be written back (gone for good once the tab closes); afterDurableSave reindexes/re-embeds/broadcasts on C while the main window shows D1; the write is watcher-suppressed (write_gate.rs:256-257 + watcher_suppress TTL 2.5s) so no adopt heals it, and nothing re-reads on screen:note-saved. No banner, no .conflict sidecar, no net, no console surface in release. Refutations attempted and failed: the write is awaited and durable (not the defect), no lock/chain/cascade/reseed gate separates discard from the in-flight write, read_note takes no lock, and nothing downstream reports the mismatch. The interleaving is not speculative - noteModel.ts:551-562 records it as a race already hit (PJ-207 section 15), which closed the savedVersion-poisoning half and left the disk half unannounced. One wording inaccuracy in the candidate: markSaved/noteDiskSynced return void, so saveUnchained never "detects" the break - it is blind to it; the same silence by another route, and the fix is the same (compare r.gen against the live model before ratifying success, and/or serialize discardFailedSave against an in-flight save).

confirmed_findings.summary: flushIfDirty — the ONE departure choke point — still asks only M.isDirty(id), so the netUnsaved model this same commit introduced (content from the write-ahead net that disk has never had, born CLEAN by design) is never flushed by any departure, universe switch, or app close, and is not counted by the residual-dirty close marker.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A save fails (file locked by a sync agent) leaving real work only in the write-ahead net. The app restarts; restoreSessionTabs seeds the tab from the net and calls setModelDiskBaseline(t.id, trueDisk, trueDisk !== t.content) (store.ts:3815) → netUnsaved = true, version 0 === savedVersion 0, so isDirty() is false. Nothing ever schedules a write for that content: flushIfDirty returns {ok:true} immediately here, and every consumer of it does the same — flushAllDirtyTabs gates on isNoteDirty alone (store.ts:3546), flushAllForAppClose selects and re-scans on isNoteDirty alone (store.ts:3571/3574) and its residual journal marker counts only isNoteDirty (store.ts:3577), while closeTab/openNoteTab/loadTabHistoryEntry/renameItem all route through flushOutgoing → flushIfDirty. PJ-207 §15 taught four other arbiters to ask hasUnsavedRecovery alongside isNoteDirty (store.ts:1139, 1344, 4950; NoteEditor.svelte:444) and left these. So the user sees their recovered paragraph on screen indefinitely, no banner (saveHealth is in-memory and died with the previous process), no autosave, no departure flush, no close marker — and the only remaining copy is the localStorage write-ahead net that PJ-110 already proved non-durable (leveldb orphan-wipe). One wipe and the work is gone with no trace that anything was ever unwritten.
confirmed_findings.reason: Grounded in the code: flushIfDirty (noteSession.ts:299) gates solely on M.isDirty(id), and a restore-seeded recovery model is clean by construction — setDiskBaseline sets only m.netUnsaved (noteModel.ts:515) and never bumps version, so version 0 === savedVersion 0. Reachable state: a save fails (locked .md), the net-before-write copy survives in constellation-wab, the app restarts, and restoreSessionTabs seeds the tab from the net and calls setModelDiskBaseline(t.id, trueDisk, trueDisk !== t.content) (store.ts:3815) → netUnsaved = true, isDirty = false. From that moment NOTHING attempts durability: flushIfDirty returns {ok:true} immediately, so every departure route through flushOutgoing (closeTab / openNoteTab / loadTabHistoryEntry / renameItem) is a no-op; flushAllDirtyTabs gates on isNoteDirty alone (store.ts:3546); flushAllTabsInLibrary skips on !isNoteDirty (store.ts:1707); flushAllForAppClose builds `dirty` from isNoteDirty and EARLY-RETURNS at store.ts:3573 when it is empty — so it never even reaches the residual journal_frontend_marker (3577), leaving zero forensic trace; and the ~10s auto-retry (+layout.svelte:1764) iterates get(saveHealth).keys(), which is empty because saveHealth is an in-memory writable (store.ts:422) that died with the previous process — and retrySaveFailure would refuse anyway (`if (!isNoteDirty(tab.id)) { clearSaveFailure; return; }`, store.ts:522). I read restoreSessionTabs (3730–3830) and the tab rendering in +layout.svelte: there is no recovery banner, toast, or unsaved-tab indicator, so the user sees an apparently normal note. Refutation attempts all fail: the four sibling guards this same commit added (adoptDisk 607, reloadTabsFromDisk 1139, watcher conflict 1344, force-re-seed 4950, snapshot flag NoteEditor:444) protect the NET, not durability — they keep the exposure alive indefinitely rather than closing it; MIG-100 Gate #8 constrains the restore itself and does not explain why every later departure, universe switch and app close also decline; and only a user keystroke (version++) can self-correct it, which the user has no cue to make. Net result: permanent, unsurfaced screen↔disk divergence whose only copy is the localStorage write-ahead net that PJ-110 already proved non-durable (and whose setWriteAhead swallows quota exceptions with an empty catch, store.ts:359). Severity MED rather than APP-KILLER because no in-app path destroys the copy — loss requires an additional external eviction event — but the window is unbounded and completely silent.

confirmed_findings.summary: On a note switch the cockpit re-renders the NEW note's title/body instantly but keeps the PREVIOUS note's backlinks, outgoing links and review/gauge stats until two async IPCs resolve — and the `loading` flag it computes is never rendered, so there is no cue.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note A is focused in the main window; the SS cockpit shows A centred with A's wings and A's gauge deck (maturity, word count, review-due). The user clicks note B in the main window → `editorPanelsData` re-emits → `shown` becomes B in the same DOM flush, so the header shows B's name and the lens gets `content=B.content`. The path-change branch (line 108) calls `fetchLinks(B)` but NOTHING clears `backlinks` (line 64), `outgoing` (line 65) or `review` (line 66) first; the clear at line 107 only runs when the path is EMPTY. For the whole duration of `get_backlink_rows` + `get_outgoing_rows` (normally ms, but seconds whenever a reindex/backfill holds the search.db connection) the second screen displays note B at the centre with note A's entire link graph and A's health gauges under B's title. `loading` is set at line 76 and cleared at line 91 but appears nowhere in the markup (lines 130-183), so nothing on screen says the picture is stale. Worse, the picture is actionable: clicking a wing node calls onNavigate → SecondScreenPage.cockpitNavigate → sendNoteToMain, so the user opens one of A's neighbours in the main window believing they followed a link of B's. Fix shape: clear backlinks/outgoing/review at the top of the path-changed branch (and render the existing `loading` flag).
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at source. In SecondScreenCockpit.svelte the fetch $effect (lines 99-110) clears backlinks/outgoing ONLY on the empty-path branch (line 107); the path-changed branch (line 108) calls fetchLinks() while backlinks (64), outgoing (65) and review (66) still hold the PREVIOUS note's rows — and `review` is never cleared on any branch. Meanwhile `shown` is $derived from the focus prop, which SecondScreenPage.svelte:1226-1234 rebuilds (path, name, content) in the same DOM flush, so the header name (144), dir (141) and the lens `content=` (168/170/172) become note B synchronously. The blend is rendered, not merely held: cockpitGraphData.ts:124-165 deriveStats builds ONE stats object from B's frontmatter (stage/stratum/tags/created, 125-137) plus A's index data (maturity 139, word_count 140, reviewState 142-147, typeMix/supports/contradicts/loadBearing/totalIn/totalOut 149-164), rendered by NoteGaugeDeck.svelte:23,55. The default lens is 'butterfly' (cockpitFlag.ts:36), which mounts that deck, and COCKPIT_ENABLED=true mounts the cockpit unconditionally — so this is the default, always-reachable path. The window is perceptible, not sub-frame: get_backlink_rows/get_outgoing_rows (cache.rs:602/653) are lock-free with_read_conn readers (ms), but get_note_review_status (review.rs:537-545) takes state.db.lock() — the WRITER mutex — and is only issued after the links await resolves (line 87); search.rs:11479-11482 documents in-tree that a single-note reindex holds db.lock() for ~5s, so a switch landing during a reindex/backfill leaves A's maturity, word count and review-due pill under B's title for seconds. It is silent: both fetch paths .catch to a silent fallback, and `loading` (set 76, cleared 91) appears nowhere in the markup (I read the full template, 130-183). Nothing self-corrects visibly — the deck simply redraws with no indication the prior reading was another note's. Charter class 2 explicitly covers on-screen content acquiring another note's data on cross-note/second-screen transitions. Severity capped at MED, not higher: the cockpit is strictly read-only (ck-ro chip, line 162) — no disk write, no search.db write, no index divergence; the worst enabled action is onNavigate → cockpitNavigate → sendNoteToMain (SecondScreenPage.svelte:195-201), which only opens a note in the main window (recoverable, non-mutating). Fix: clear backlinks, outgoing AND review at the top of the pathChanged branch, and render the existing `loading` flag.

confirmed_findings.summary: The cockpit asks for backlinks with `aliases: []`, while the main window passes the note's real aliases (+layout.svelte:1951), so every alias-routed backlink is silently missing from the second-screen knowledge graph.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note "Île-de-France" carries alias "IDF" (frontmatter or rename-stamped). Ten notes link it as [[IDF]]. The main window's Backlinks panel calls `get_backlink_rows` with `aliases: aliasesForActive` (+layout.svelte:1951) and shows all ten. The cockpit hard-codes `aliases: []` at line 80 and then re-filters with `getBacklinks(blRows, name, undefined, [])` at line 84 (store.ts:5716 only widens the target set when noteAliases is non-empty), so the second screen renders the note with those ten backlinks absent — no error, no empty-state note, just a smaller graph than the same note shows one screen over. The user reads the cockpit as the note's relationship picture and concludes the alias-linked notes are unconnected. Rule-8 divergence: a derived surface silently out of step with the [[wikilink]] truth in the .md files.
confirmed_findings.reason:
Verified end-to-end against the actual code and the Boss's live universe DB.

MECHANISM (read, not inferred):
- src-tauri/src/cache.rs:602-643 `get_backlink_rows` builds `targets = [lower(note_name)] + aliases` and matches note_links against that set. With `aliases: []` the target set is the primary name ONLY — alias-routed rows are excluded by the SQL itself, so no later widening is possible.
- src/lib/libraries/store.ts:5699-5717 `getBacklinks(rows, name, decay, noteAliases)` only adds to the target set when `noteAliases` is non-empty, so the cockpit's second `[]` at line 84 is also a no-op.
- src/lib/components/SecondScreenCockpit.svelte:80 hard-codes `aliases: []`; the resulting `backlinks` feeds every lens (lines 168-174: Butterfly / Ledger / Orrery / Radial). This is the only backlink call site besides the alias-aware one at src/routes/+layout.svelte:1951, which passes `notePathToAliases.get(tabPath)`.
- Root cause is structural, not a typo: `EditorPanelsData` (src/lib/secondScreen.ts:352-359) carries only path/name/libraryName/libraryPath/content — no aliases — so the second-screen window has no alias data at all (grep for "alias" in SecondScreenPage.svelte: zero hits).

REACHABILITY: the cockpit mounts unconditionally for a focused note (SecondScreenPage.svelte:1225-1233); `COCKPIT_ENABLED` gates only the §10/§14 zones, not the graph. No flag stands between the user and this.

MAGNITUDE (measured on a read-only copy of E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge\.constellation\search.db): note_aliases holds 1,583 rows (1,435 frontmatter + 148 rename-stamped) across 1,482 notes; 23,269 non-archived note_links rows reach 412 notes via an alias different from the note's own name. After the dedupe-by-source getBacklinks applies, distinct backlink SOURCES rendered by the cockpit vs the main window for the same note:
  "Europe in the middle ages" (alias "middle ages") — 1 vs 338 (337 missing)
  "Roman period" (alias "roman empire") — 9 vs 368 (359 missing)
  "Byzantine" (alias "byzantine empire") — 62 vs 333 (271 missing)
  "Ancient Greek language" (alias "ancient greek") — 446 vs 753 (307 missing)

WHY NOT REFUTED: the `.catch(() => [])` swallows nothing here — the IPC succeeds and returns a set that is truthfully alias-free, so there is no error to surface. No empty-state, no count, no cue; the graph just draws fewer wings. It never self-corrects — every refetch (path change, 450 ms nonce refetch, save/reindex) re-sends `[]`. The gen-guard, path-guard and onDestroy cleanup are all sound and irrelevant to this defect.

SEVERITY: MED, not APP-KILLER. Nothing is written; no .md and no index row is corrupted; the [[wikilink]] truth on disk is intact — this is a read-only derived surface silently out of step with it (Rule-8 divergence). But the divergence is not marginal: on the surface whose whole concept is "the open note's relationship picture," the user sees 1 connection where 338 exist one screen over, and concludes those notes are unconnected.

FIX SHAPE: aliases must reach the SS window — either add `aliases: string[]` to EditorPanelsData populated from `notePathToAliases` at the emit site, or have `get_backlink_rows` resolve the note's aliases server-side from note_aliases given the path. Whole-Ecosystem check done: these are the only two get_backlink_rows call sites in the codebase.

confirmed_findings.summary: followExternalRename/followPeek move the second screen's tab path and title but never refresh its CONTENT, and the channel the comment defers to ('screen:note-saved') is never emitted for a rename — so the SS renders the note's pre-rename frontmatter indefinitely.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The user renames an open note in the main window. rename_item rewrites that note's own title: and appends the old title to aliases on disk (store.ts:4895) under watcher suppression, so no library-changed event fires for it. The rename handler emits only note-renamed (+layout.svelte:7588) and the cascade emits cascade:rewrote carrying result.rewritten — the REFERRER notes whose wikilinks were rewritten (libraries.rs:7080-7083), which does not include the renamed note itself. broadcastNoteSaved is never called for a rename. The SS's new onRenamed handler therefore repaths the tab and updates its label while tab.content and the model keep the pre-rename bytes: the second screen shows the NEW name in the tab bar and the OLD title/aliases in the note body and property surfaces, permanently, with nothing indicating the display is stale. (Read-only window, so no disk damage — the damage is on-screen content that no longer matches the file.)
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, silent, reachable — but display-only. Verified end to end: (1) rename_item (libraries.rs:1755-1789) rewrites the renamed note's OWN frontmatter (title + old title appended to aliases) through gate_rmw_rename, and write_gate.rs:256-257/:737-738 watcher-suppress the temp/final/parent/rename paths (TTL 2.5s, watcher_suppress.rs:27), so no library-changed reaches the SS for that file. (2) The only cross-window signal is emitNoteRenamed at +layout.svelte:7588; broadcastNoteSaved exists only in NoteEditor's save handlers (never on the rename path — renameItem's flush calls saveNoteSession directly in store.ts), and cascade:rewrote carries result.rewritten, i.e. the REFERRER notes, not the renamed note. So no channel delivers the renamed note's new bytes to the SS. (3) The SS's onRenamed (SecondScreenPage.svelte:150-153) → followExternalRename (store.ts:1196-1209) updates only {path, name} + repathNoteModel; it never touches tab.content and never bumps reloadVersion, and noteSession.ensure (noteSession.ts:67-72) returns early because the model's path now matches, so the model keeps its pre-rename props. (4) The rendered properties come from tab.content (NoteEditor.svelte:137-140 → properties={parsed.properties}/rawYaml at :808-809) while the heading uses tab.name (:795, updated) — so in the SS note-companion branch (SecondScreenPage.svelte:1397-1421) the header shows the NEW name while Properties shows title: <old> and aliases without the stamped old title, indefinitely and with nothing surfaced. The inline comment at :145 defers to 'screen:note-saved', a channel that never fires for a rename — the drift is in the code's own stated contract. Escalation refuted: every SS mount passes ssReadOnly=true and NoteEditor returns early on readOnly at :208/:285/:378/:478/:558/:703 and gates editBody at :820, so the stale model can never compose or write — disk is never diverged, only the on-screen copy. It heals silently on the next screen:note-saved/library-changed for that path via adoptFreshDiskIntoSS (:610-640, clean model adopts + reloadVersion bump), on universe switch, or on SS restart. Reachability is narrow (the branch needs editorPanelsActive=false — main with no active tab per +layout.svelte:738-746 — plus contextMode!=='skyview' and mainSidebarMode!=='tree'), but it is reachable and the stale bytes persist across branch switches until an adopt fires. Fix is one line in the SS onRenamed: await adoptFreshDiskIntoSS(newPath) after followExternalRename.
